newsitem.title: JAPAN: LME copper edges higher in Asia, market quiet.
newsitem.headline: LME copper edges higher in Asia, market quiet.

text.p: London Metal Exchange copper prices edged higher during Asian trading hours on Wednesday, modestly extending overnight gains, while the other metals were largely stagnant in quiet dealings, traders said.
Copper received a modest lift in New York overnight after an announcement by Asarco that mine and smelter production at Southern Peru Copper had been temporarily halted due to flooding.

Prior to that, LME prices had rallied during London trade to fresh recent highs, although, with the exception of zinc which remained buoyant after hitting a 4-1/2-year high, the other metals subsequently retraced and ended Tuesday's afternoon kerb lower.

Traders in Japan said the latest gains in metal prices seemed to be fuelled largely by speculative buying, and while they believed further near-term gains were possible, especially in zinc and aluminium, they said the markets were due for a correction in the intermediate term.
One trade house source expected three-month aluminium to make a try for $1,750 a tonne before correcting.
At 0745 GMT, LME benchmark three-month copper was bid at $2,410 a tonne versus $2,405 at 1900 GMT on Tuesday and the afternoon kerb close of $2,395.
Aluminium was bid at $1,689 a tonne, up slightly from $1,685 at 1900 GMT on Tuesday and the afternoon kerb close of $1,686.
